questions.q: A chromatogram of a food colouring shows three spots; one matches E133 (Rf 0.62). Describe how to carry out the experiment and how to identify E133.
questions.a: Pencil start line (1); spots above solvent level (1); lid on, solvent rises (1); measure spot and front distances, Rf = spot ÷ front (1); matching Rf (and position) to a known sample identifies E133 (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes the first two points: 'Draw a pencil line 1 cm from the bottom (pencil does not dissolve). Spot the colouring on the line and stand the paper in solvent below the line.'

questions.q: Explain why graphite is used for electrodes and as a lubricant.
questions.a: Delocalised electrons carry charge (1); layers held by weak forces (1) slide over each other (1).

questions.q: Explain why the boiling points of simple molecules increase with relative molecular mass.
questions.a: Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces (1), so more energy is needed to separate them (1).

questions.q: Explain why sodium chloride conducts when molten but not when solid.
questions.a: Solid: ions fixed in the lattice (1); molten: ions free to move and carry charge (1).
questions.model: Solid state: where are the ions? Fixed in the lattice, so they cannot move. Molten: ions free to move, so they carry charge through the liquid.

questions.q: A pure substance melts at a sharp temperature. What does a mixture do?
questions.a: Melts over a range of temperatures.

questions.q: Draw (describe) the dot-and-cross diagram for HCl.
questions.a: One shared pair between H and Cl (1); Cl has three non-bonding pairs, outer shells shown (1).

questions.q: Which conducts electricity as a solid?
Big question: why does diamond not conduct but graphite does?
questions.a: Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; in diamond all outer electrons are in bonds.
